message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note** – “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to handle host maintenance (TERMINATE = stop VM) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs on first boot |

> **Tip** – If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` values accordingly.

---

## 2.  REST API call (for programmatic use)

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

### Steps to use the REST call

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope  
   `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.
2. Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your values.
3. Send the request (e.g., via `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client).

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| Project ID | `PROJECT_ID` |
| Zone | `us-central1-a` (or your preferred zone) |
| Machine type | `n1-standard-8` (or other) |
| GPU | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| OS | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| Disk | 200 GB SSD (adjust size) |
| Auth | OAuth 2.0 token with Compute scope |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
